title: Quantization-driven hiring offset analysis
body:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory doc to estimate how model quantization improvements (2-bit/4-bit paths, new kernel swaps) could reduce hosted GPU spend and whether that delta meaningfully offsets near-term hiring needs in ops/infra. Not a final finance model; draft for FY27 planning conversation with Eng and Product.

High-level thesis:
- If we can safely move a portion of serving workload to more aggressive quantized execution without URF-quality regressions, token-level infra cost drops materially (GPU time tokens).
- Lower infra burn reduces the runway pressure and may delay or reduce immediate hires on serving/runtime teams by allowing reallocation of headcount to higher-priority sprints.
- We need scenario-based sensitivity rather than a single number: quality/regression risk and rollout time are the biggest uncertainties.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline monthly hosted GPU bill for inference (prod): $1,800,000 (all regions).
- Weighted average model mix: 60% L=2k calls, 30% L=8k, 10% L=32k (by token share).
- Current serving efficiency baseline: FP16 on A100-like instances.
- Average tokens-per-month (prod): 420B tokens.
- Average effective cost per 1M tokens (baseline): $4.29.

Quantization scenarios (conservative / aggressive / optimistic):
1) Conservative (4-bit rollout on 30% of volume): 18% infra cost reduction on covered volume -> net infra drop = 0.30 * 0.18 = 5.4% -> monthly savings ~$97k
2) Aggressive (4-bit + kernel tuning on 60% of volume): 30% reduction on covered -> net infra drop = 18% -> monthly savings ~$324k
3) Optimistic (mixed 2-bit fast paths for short context + 4-bit for long): 45% reduction on 70% of volume -> net infra drop = 0.315 -> monthly savings ~$567k

Mapping infra savings to headcount offset (simple approach):
- Target role: Serving/runtime SRE/Eng (mid-SWE fully loaded cost = $32k / month).
- Hiring lead time: 10–12 weeks. Contractors cost premium 1.6x.

Offset outcomes (monthly savings -> approximate FTE equivalents):
- Conservative: $97k / $32k = ~3.0 FTE-months -> can delay ~3 hires for 1 month or 1 hire for ~3 months
- Aggressive: $324k / $32k = ~10.1 FTE-months -> ~3 hires delayed 3 months, or 1 hire covered for ~10 months
- Optimistic: $567k / $32k = ~17.7 FTE-months -> ~5 hires delayed for 3 months, or 2 hires for ~8 months

Sensitivity notes and non-linearities:
- Quality/regression risk: If even 5% of revenue-impacting requests need fallback to original model, measured cost savings drop faster than linear due to tail requests keeping larger clusters hot.
- Regional capacity: Savings concentrate in US-west/eu-west where we have scale; smaller regions see little immediate benefit. Headcount in regional ops may not be offset.
- Onboarding and maintenance overhead: New quant paths increase complexity and could generate ~0.3 FTE ongoing maintenance burden per major quant path (approx $3.2k / month per path).

Risks and caveats:
- Savings assume no pricing/contract step-down for GPU capacity (if cloud spot prices rise, net savings shrink).
- Product SLA constraints may prevent aggressive rollout on high-SLA customer tiers; may only apply to self-serve volume.
- Migration timeline: conservative 3–4 months to implement + 2 months of canary. Aggressive ~6–9 months. Optimistic requires risky lifts and deep infra changes (9–12+ months).

Actionable recommendations (short list):
- Finance: include a quantization sensitivity band in FY27 headcount planning (conservative/aggressive/optimistic) and treat savings as contingent until canary passes.
- Eng/Product: prioritize a 30% volume pilot on non-SLA, low-rewrite workloads with strict canaries and metrics (latency, artifact regression, sampling QA). Goal: get to Conservative by end of Q3 2026.
- Ops: create a rollback cost model to measure fallback friction; instrument tail hotspot costs separately.
- Hiring: adopt a 12-week rolling hiring hold trigger: if conservative savings are realized for 2 consecutive months, postpone next tranche of 2 mid-SWE hires by 8–12 weeks.

Open questions for next sync:
- Which customer segments can we safely target for pilot? (sales input needed)
- Are there existing vendor discounts or spot commitments that change the marginal savings? (finance vendor team to check)
- Legal/compliance risk on quantized outputs for regulated customers? (sec/compliance)

Appendix: quick numbers snapshot (rounded)
- Monthly baseline infra: $1.8M
- Conservative savings: $97k/mo (~5.4%)
- Aggressive savings: $324k/mo (~18%)
- Optimistic savings: $567k/mo (~31.5%)
- Mid-SWE fully loaded per-month: $32k

Notes to self: collect real token distribution by route (api keys) and run model-by-model microbenchmarks (cost per 1M tokens under each quant path) before converting this to formal FY27 budget play. Slack thread: #eng-costs -> "quant-savings-pilot".

End of draft.
notes: Informal draft, numbers rough — intended to seed cross-functional planning. Will attach Microbench CSV after running infra experiments.
